Nato’s Rutte got a question on Russia’s demands to rewrite the European security order as part of the Ukraine peace settlement. “We are all totally clear that the proposals Russia put forward in 2021, basically going back to … for Nato to basically move backwards from where we are now and to the 1997, borders are unacceptable. And there’s nobody in Nato who thinks this is a good idea.”
Rutte also gets pushed a bit on the Polish incident last week, as he says: “It is clear that this is a dangerous incident. It comes from Russia. Whether it is intentional or not has to be decided, of course, by authorities. I will never speculate. I can only comment on that when we have the evidence coming out of, of the system, where Poland and other Nato allies work together to assess what exactly happened.”
---
Over in Berlin, Rutte is still diplomatically answering questions from national delegations and avoiding many any news. So far his most entertaining line was about making sure he never forgets to mention Italy as a key Nato ally, because he doesn’t want to fight Italy’s defence minister, Guido Crosetto. “If I would ever forget about Italy, then the defence minister, Guido Crossetto, whom you don’t want to get into a fight with given his build, will remind me quite forcefully, I can assure you.”
---
Elsewhere, I’m also keeping an eye on reports from Denmark and Germany, where hundreds of schools have received emails containing bomb threats. The German tabloid Bild reported that investigators do not consider the threats credible, as they are looking into where they came from. The latest incidents come after weeks of similar scares across Europe, which have also disrupted some European flights. I will keep an eye on this for you.
---
Meanwhile, Rutte is still answering questions at Nato’s parliamentary assembly – on the Arctic security and the expected review of US force posture in Europe, among others – but he’s bravely avoiding saying anything remotely new so far. I will keep monitoring his speech.
---
Meanwhile, Albania has strongly denied suggestions that the naval drone attack against the Russian warship in Libya originated from its territory. “The reports in question are inaccurate and do not reflect the facts. Albania was not involved in this incident, and its territory was neither used nor made available for the launch or facilitation of such an attack,” Albania’s ministry of foreign affairs said. It added: “We categorically reject these allegations, which have been presented without verifiable evidence. We call on those responsible for disseminating them to correct the record and to exercise accuracy, due diligence and responsibility when reporting on matters of such sensitivity.”
---
Turning to Ukraine, Nato’s Rutte stresses the need to secure the flow of “crucial supplies” or air defence weapons and ammunition to Ukraine. “It helps Ukraine to defend itself today, but it also strengthens Ukraine’s hands in any future negotiations with Russia. … But support needs to be concrete. We have to show Putin that his attempts to weaken our support will fail.” He also stresses the need to offer broader support to Ukraine, as well as build the resilience of Nato societies against any potential acts of sabotage against critical infrastructure. “Our citizens need to know that the lights will stay on, that their homes will stay warm, that hospitals, transport and communications will keep working.” He then wraps up with a point about the value of democratic societies and why Nato rivals fear that freedom most. And we go into the Q&A.
---
Nato’s Rutte is speaking now, calling for “action and real leadership” in Nato’s response to growing threats from China, Iran, Russia and North Korea, and “intensifying malign activities targeting our nations.” “One day it can be in the form of an arson attack against a factory or drones disrupt disrupting an airport. The next, it is sabotaged railways or cargo vessels targeted at sea and cyber-attacks.” Rutte specificially references “the dangerous incident in Poland on Friday,” and “some serious stuff happening on the Black Sea” prompting Nato to look at the regional security more closely with Bulgaria, Romania and Turkey. “It’s all happening now, and it won’t go away anytime soon. … The conclusion of all of this is that we are all targeted, that we are all affected – when it comes to our pipelines, our cables, our energy grids and our economies – and they are all interconnected. … That means that we are all in this for the long term, and therefore we must step up to the plate, to en

Nato’s secretary general Mark Rutte is about to speak at Nato’s parliamentary assembly meeting in Berlin. I will follow his speech for any interesting lines on Ukraine, Nato’s security and the state of alliance given Trump’s ‘friendship’ with Russia’s Putin.

And Ukraine’s SBU has also offered more photos showing the attack…
---
Meanwhile, Ukraine’s SBU security service also commented on the sinking of the Russian warship in Libya. It said the corvette “regularly escorted enemy maritime convoys” and was part of Russia’s Black Sea Fleet. “A Ka-27 multipurpose helicopter was on board the corvette and also sank,” the SBU said. There was no immediate comment from Russia about the strikes.
---
Zelenskyy also said that “partners” – presumably the US – want the fourway talks between Ukraine, Russia, the US and Europe to take place before Christmas. “We are ready to do this literally tomorrow. We have heard from our partners that they want to try to make it happen before Christmas. We hope it happens sooner, and we must come to this meeting with a clear agenda, prepared and agreed by all of us.” He added: “When the main question comes up, ‘what happens after this war?’, our common answer must be security. Real security. Security for Ukraine, security for all of Russia’s neighbours, security for Europe and the entire Euro-Atlantic area. This is only possible if we work together as closely as possible. I believe this is only possible when Russia has no temptation to test whether security guarantees really work with Nato.”
---
In the last half hour, Volodymyr Zelenskyy addressed the Nato parliamentary Assembly meeting in Berlin.
He warned that “Russian aggression has shown that when Ukraine is left out, and when there is no clear understanding of how Europe should be protected, anything can happen.” He also celebrated overnight strikes against Russia, saying Ukraine “keep finding ways to get back on our feet after every Russian attack.” “Today, Russia can feel our response all the way from western Siberia, where its oil refiners are burning, to the coast of Libya, where its warships are sinking.” Zelenskyy stressed that Ukraine has repeatedly offered “steps to reduce the fighting,” and “never been the ones to raise the stakes,” but Russia “still gives us no peaceful response.” He urged Nato leaders to “invest in stronger security and greater resilience,” saying “does anyone here still believe that one day Russia will simply become peaceful and safe again?” “Just look at the last, last 100 years of Russian hi

---
Ukraine’s president Volodymyr Zelenskyy has claimed responsibility for sinking a Russian warship at a Libyan naval base on Sunday, saying it was part of Kyiv’s response to Russia’s continuing aggression.
“An exemplary Ukrainian operation in response to Russia’s war,” he said in a post on X, with a video showing the moment the corvette was hit by Ukrainian drones. “Our warriors deployed seven Ukrainian-made naval drones. Despite all the enemy’s efforts to counter the attack, the Russian corvette Merkury was sunk. It’s one of their newest ships, commissioned in 2023, during the full-scale war,” he said. Zelenskyy added that a Russian dry cargo vessel MV Angara, which he said was used for transporting weapons, was also sunk.
